blast_radius_assessment.verdict: correct semantics per ADR rev-2 §10.1/§10.3 truth-table — NOT an over-reach
blast_radius_assessment.changed_asserts: FF-DC3 (`name` now absent for both readers), FF-DC7 masked-value test (`name` absent), FF-DC7 null-clearance test (`name` absent), and the maskFields null-clearance test (`name` absent). In every one of these the resource is GOVERNED (a classified field like ssn/card is present), and `name` has no classification row for the requested version.
blast_radius_assessment.adjudication: ADR §10.1 row 4 (governed, version has rows but not for f) and the binding decision rule in §10.1 ('In state G, a field with no resolvable class for the handle's version fails closed to maximal masking ... the version boundary is fail-closed for the WHOLE facet') REQUIRE exactly this: under governance, a no-row field drops, it is not kept raw. So `name` dropping is the ADR-mandated answer, not a coder over-reach. The over-reach hypothesis (governed should bite ONLY classified fields, leaving non-classified raw) is the very ambiguity §10.1 names as the R-1 root cause: the model has NO per-field is-classified signal independent of row-presence, so 'genuinely unclassified field (raw correct)' is structurally indistinguishable from 'classified field whose row is missing for this version (must fail-closed)'. Resolving that doubt toward raw is the original bug; resolving it toward drop is fail-closed (NF-3).
blast_radius_assessment.spec_vs_adr_alignment: ALIGNED, not divergent. SPEC AC-4 ('a classified facet whose facet_schema_version has no matching rows yields maximal masking; the field does not leak raw') + AC-12 (version boundary = AC-4) + the spec §1 red-line and FR/NF text 'a facet whose schema version has no classification rows is fail-closed (treated as maximally-masked), never widened' and 'a facet-schema-version mismatch resolves to MORE masking, never less'. The spec frames the unit as the FACET (treated as maximally-masked), and 'does not leak raw' is the value-suppression intent the rev-1 code inverted. Whole-governed-facet fail-closed satisfies AC-4/AC-12 strictly more conservatively and never widens beyond the grant-conferred visibleFields (the upstream grant facet still caps the field set). No spec AC is violated by the wider drop; the additive-floor compatibility for genuinely ungoverned resources is preserved by state U (FF-DC4a). Conclusion: the blast radius is principle-consistent and in-bounds.
